data.head: ## Measurements on the dev host (probes in the session scratchpad, every process they started ended by them)

body: - **The outer-PTY path (`orphan_probe.py`):** a holder process opened a PTY, started `target/debug/viola --home <scratch home> run builder -- target/debug/viola-fake-agent --screens …` on its slave in a new session, drained the master; the parent SIGKILLed the holder 2 s after the snapshot named a child. 5 s later the wrapper and the fake agent were both gone (`/proc/<pid>` absent). Reading: the master's close hangs up the slave, the session leader (the wrapper) takes SIGHUP's default action, and its inner PTY's close ends the fake agent.

- **The piped path (`orphan_probe_pipe.py`):** the same start on three pipes, the holder SIGKILLed. 5 s later the wrapper stood `S` on `__futex_wait`, 0 % CPU over 5.0 s, six threads asleep (`viola`, `channel-accept`, `heartbeat`, three unnamed); the fake agent `S` on `wait_woken`, 0 % CPU. Both were then ended by the probe's own SIGKILL. Reading: a wrapper whose test is gone and that holds no terminal lives on with its child, idle.

- **The supervisor path, from the code:** `supervise.rs:96-98` loops on `stop_requested` every `POLL`; a SIGKILLed test writes no `stop.request`, so the supervisor and every wrapper under its outer PTYs live on, the supervisor idle.

- The CI red: VERIFIED against ci#44048204364 (sha 668854a6, `test (ubuntu-latest)`), the mechanism re-derived. _Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-17-booted-wrapper-does-not-outlive-its-test · **Version:** viola-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-17T09:47:08Z

First, close HEAD's CI red (CARRY `cry-n25qin7l`, the directive's item 2, `inputs#I1`). P3 measured its mechanism
against ci#44048204364 (research §Scope premise closure). rust-cache at the pinned `6323deb` strips every file under a
non-profile directory of `target/` before it saves. So a restored `target/e2e-home/viola-stamp-<key>/` comes back with
its folders and none of its files. On identical source the key matches, and `stamp_dir`
(`tests/support/home.rs:395`) trusts `is_dir()` and copies an empty tree. The fix makes the stamp count only by its
files. A stamp that has none gets a fresh stamp in the next generation dir, and nothing is removed (the overseer's
answer to the P4 fork, `inputs#I2`: no fifth removal way, so security-plan
`(security-plan · security-anti-patterns/decision/test-removal-own-dirs-only)` stands as it is). The proof is this
chunk's own pre-CI push. The overseer's re-run saved the key `…-058865c8` again (`inputs#I3`), so that push hits it
exactly, and it reads green only if the fixture no longer trusts a hollow stamp.

Second, a wrapper a test boots, and the agent under it, end when that test ends, whether it passes, fails, times out
or is SIGKILLed (v2-37; test-plan `(test-plan · integration-test-strategy/decision/wrapper-drop-guard)` is a `Drop`
guard, which a SIGKILL never runs). P3 measured three boot paths. Under the root fixture chain's outer PTY the test
holds the master, so a killed test hangs the wrapper's terminal up and both processes end. On pipes or a direct spawn
the wrapper and its fake agent live on, idle. Under an in-test harness session the supervisor lives on until a
`stop.request` that never comes. The two surviving paths are tied to the test. Every root-test spawn of a long-lived
viola child goes through one shared helper (test-plan `(test-plan · test-strategy/decision/one-shared-test-helper)`)
that sets the kernel's parent-death signal on the child. The harness supervisor an in-test session spawns is tied the
same way, and its death hangs up every wrapper's outer PTY. The CLI `boot`'s supervisor stays an ordinary child that
outlives `boot` (`(test-plan · 5-command-implementation/decision/supervisor-ordinary-child)`).

Third, the proof of «killed» (the directive's item 4). A test owns a victim process, a self-spawn of its own test
binary, which boots a wrapper by each path and reports the pids. The test SIGKILLs the victim, censuses the victim's
whole recorded tree by pid and start time, and reads it gone within `WITHIN`. No product code changes and no mutation
run or live start is made (`inputs#I1` items 3–4). No test kills a process it does not own: the census kills only
recorded survivors of the test's own victim, and only on its failure path.

1. **The stamp counts only by its files** (`tests/support/home.rs`, `stamp_dir`; FIRST, the CI red).
   Split `stamp_dir` into a public wrapper and a core `stamp_dir_in(base, key, stamper)`. `base` is the e2e-home
   base, `key` the stamp key, and `stamper` the closure that stamps a home (`take_stamp` in production), so a test can
   drive the core on a temp base. Under the exclusive `viola-stamp-<key>.lock`, which it holds unchanged:
   - (a) A stamp dir counts as stamped only when its completion file `stamped` stands beside its `home/` and
     `home/ledger/stamps.json` stands. `stamped` is an empty file the core writes inside the tmp dir after `stamper`
     returns and before the rename. rust-cache's strip removes both, so a restored stamp never counts.
   - (b) The candidates are `viola-stamp-<key>` and then `viola-stamp-<key>-g<n>` for n = 1, 2, …, in that order. The
     first candidate that counts is returned. A candidate that stands but does not count is left exactly as found:
     no file in it is read, written or removed.
   - (c) If no candidate counts, the core stamps into a `.tmp-<pid>` dir of the first free name and renames it there.
     A candidate is free when nothing stands at its path. The existing dead-`.tmp-` removal stays scoped to this key's
     own prefix, as today.
   - (d) `sweep_other_stamps` is unchanged. Its prefix `viola-stamp-<other>` already covers another build's generation
     dirs, taken only by `try_lock`.
   `stamped_home` keeps its signature. Its callers are `stamped_home` itself and `stamp_home_dir` (`tests/cli_verify.rs:553`).
   Keeps tests S2 (a fresh private home per test) and the test-plan convention
   `(test-plan · test-data-fixtures/decision/stamps-only-from-verify)`: the stamp still comes only from `take_stamp`.

2. **The hollow-stamp witnesses** (`tests/cli_verify.rs`, beside `stamped_home_reuses_one_stamp_for_every_home`).
   Two cases drive `stamp_dir_in` on a temp base made by `create_private_dir`, with a counting stub stamper. The stub
   writes `home/ledger/stamps.json` through `viola verify`'s own stamping, the same `take_stamp` call (no hand-written
   stamps file).
   - (a) `stamped_home_rebuilds_a_stamp_restored_without_its_files`: the test plants `viola-stamp-<key>/home/ledger/`,
     `home/bin/` and `home/plugin/` as directories only (what rust-cache restores). The core then returns a stamp
     holding `ledger/stamps.json`, the stamper ran once, the planted tree still stands with no file added, and the
     returned path is `viola-stamp-<key>-g1/home`.
   - (b) `stamped_home_reuses_a_rebuilt_generation_without_stamping_again`: a second call on the same base returns the
     same `-g1` home and the stamper's count stays at 1.
   With step 1(a)'s file check removed, case (a) reads the planted hollow home and fails on its stamps assertion
   (control `stamp-hollow`). Keeps tests S1 (no sleep: the stub is synchronous) and S3 (naming).

3. **The tied spawn helper** (`tests/support/tied.rs`, a new module declared in `tests/support/mod.rs`).
   - `tie(&mut Command) -> &mut Command`: records the test process's pid, then through `CommandExt::pre_exec` makes
     the child set `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGKILL)` and exit at once when `getppid()` no longer equals the recorded
     pid (the parent died between the fork and the prctl). Each `unsafe` carries a SAFETY comment: async-signal-safe
     calls only.
   - `viola() -> Command`: `Command::new(VIOLA)`, tied.
   - The kernel sends the signal when the spawning THREAD ends. The doc comment says so, and every caller spawns on
     the test's own thread or on a thread that outlives its child.
   - libc is already a root dependency (`Cargo.toml:152`), so no manifest changes.
   - The census helper `recorded_tree(pid) -> Vec<(u32, String)>`: every descendant of `pid` read from
     `/proc/*/stat`'s ppid field, with its start time through sysinfo, as the shared support's `wrapper_pid` reads
     processes (`tests/support/home.rs:1089`). And `gone_within(tree)`: polls under `Watch` until no recorded
     (pid, start time) pair runs, bounded by `WITHIN`. On its deadline it kills each recorded survivor whose pid and
     start time still match (the test's own tree, nothing else) and then panics, naming the survivors' count by
     subject (wrapper / agent / supervisor), no pid.

5. **The in-test supervisor is tied** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs`, `session.rs`,
   `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs`).
   - `BootOptions` gains `tied: bool`.
   - `spawn_supervisor` takes it. When true, the supervisor's `Command` sets the same parent-death signal and parent
     check in `pre_exec`, and so does `boot`'s stamping `viola verify` Command (`boot.rs:229`).
   - `harness_session` (`session.rs:60`) passes `tied: true`; the CLI `boot` in `viola-harness.rs` passes
     `tied: false`, so `agent-run boot`'s supervisor still outlives `boot`.
   - A unit case in `boot.rs`'s test module, `boot_ties_its_supervisor_only_when_asked`, reads both callers' options
     through one shared constructor per caller: `BootOptions::for_session(…)` sets `tied: true` and
     `BootOptions::for_cli(…)` sets `tied: false`, and the case asserts each.

6. **The killed-test witnesses, root** (`tests/cross_killed_test.rs`, a new E2E-layer binary by its `cross_` prefix).
   - (a) `cross_killed_test_census_finds_no_untied_viola_spawn`: over every `tests/*.rs` and `tests/support/*.rs`,
     masked through `support::source_scan` (`Mask::CommentsAndLiterals`), no `Command::new(VIOLA)`,
     `Command::new(support::VIOLA)` or `Command::new(home::VIOLA)` stands outside `tests/support/tied.rs`. A planted
     known positive (a synthetic text holding one) reads one hit.
   - (b) One victim test, `killed_test_victim_entry`. With the test-only self-spawn marker `ROOT_TIED_TEST_CHILD`
     unset it returns at once. With the marker set to a report path it boots one wrapper in the mode named by its
     second line, writes the wrapper's and the child's pids from the snapshot to the report (0600, through the shared
     `Watch` report form), then parks. The modes are:
     - `piped`: `Piped::spawn` of `viola run` over `stamped_home`;
     - `direct`: `support::cli::spawn` of `viola run`;
     - `outer`: the `booted_wrapper` fixture;
     - `frozen`: `booted_wrapper` under `Frozen`.
   - (c) Four witnesses, one per mode: `killed_test_leaves_no_piped_wrapper`, `killed_test_leaves_no_direct_wrapper`,
     `killed_test_leaves_no_outer_pty_wrapper` and `killed_test_leaves_no_frozen_wrapper`. Each:
     - spawns the victim through `tied::tie` on its own test binary, `--exact killed_test_victim_entry`, the marker set,
       `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` kept (S5);
     - waits for the report within `WITHIN`;
     - takes the victim's `recorded_tree`, which must hold the wrapper and the agent the report names;
     - SIGKILLs the victim by its own `Child::kill`, reaps it, and reads `gone_within` over the recorded tree.
   - (d) `panicked_test_leaves_no_piped_wrapper`: the victim's `panic` mode boots `piped`, writes its report and
     panics. The witness reads the victim's exit non-zero and the tree gone.
   Every home lives under `target/e2e-home` (obs S1). The binary joins the `ci` stamped-home override (step 8).
   Keeps tests S1–S5, arch S1–S3 and S6, and obs S1–S3.

7. **The killed-test witness, harness** (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_tied.rs`, an integration-layer binary).
   - The victim entry `harness_victim_entry`, behind `HARNESS_TIED_TEST_CHILD` (the same form as step 6(b)), opens a
     `harness_session` with one instance. It writes the supervisor's pid (from `session.json`), the wrapper's and the
     child's pids to its report, then parks.
   - The witness `killed_test_leaves_no_harness_session` follows step 6(c)'s steps over that tree, through this
     crate's own sysinfo reads (the harness already depends on sysinfo: `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml:52`). The root
     helper is out of reach: the fixture chain exists once, in the root (`(test-plan · 5-command-implementation/decision/fixture-chain-exists-once)`).
   - The session's home and session dir stand after the kill (no `Drop` ran). The witness removes the session dir and
     the home through the harness's own `cleanup` by its session id, a test-side removal by its session name prefix.

8. **The `ci` kill line** (`.config/nextest.toml`): `binary(cross_killed_test)` joins the stamped-home 20 s override's
   filter (`[[profile.ci.overrides]]`, the second), as its comment requires of every binary that drives verify
   through the stamped-home fixture.
- `tests/support/tied.rs` — the tied spawn helper, `viola()`, the recorded-tree census and `gone_within`
- `tests/cross_killed_test.rs` — the untied-spawn census and the killed and panicked test witnesses, root
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_tied.rs` — the killed harness-session witness
- `tests/support/home.rs` — `stamp_dir` over the new core `stamp_dir_in`: counts a stamp by its files, the next generation for a hollow one
- `tests/support/mod.rs` — `pub mod tied;`
- `tests/support/piped.rs` — `Piped::spawn` ties its command
- `tests/support/cli.rs` — `spawn` through `tied::viola()`
- `tests/support/start.rs` — its viola spawns through `tied::viola()`
- `tests/support/verify.rs` — its viola spawns through `tied::viola()`
- `tests/cli_verify.rs` — the two hollow-stamp witnesses
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs` — `BootOptions.tied`, the tied supervisor and stamping spawns, the unit case
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/session.rs` — `harness_session` asks for a tied supervisor

No boot-path touchpoint: the product binary is unchanged, so there is no `smoke` entry. No live leg (`inputs#I1`
item 3) and no mutation run (item 4). The fake agent's screens are unchanged, and `cli_verify` is in the block anyway,

**Section:** 3. Test Harness Contract
**Change:** ~ decision/supervisor-ordinary-child · rule: was «The supervisor is spawned as an ordinary child with no detach flags, outlives boot, and stops only through its stop request.»; now «The supervisor is spawned as an ordinary child with no detach flags and outlives boot; the agent-run CLI boot leaves it untied, stopping only through its stop request, while an in-test harness session ties it and its stamping viola verify to the test thread by a parent-death kill.»
**Why:** decision/supervisor-ordinary-child: An in-test harness session's supervisor now dies with its test thread, so the row's claim that the supervisor stops only through its stop request holds for the CLI boot alone.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-17T12-01-09Z-wrap/

- **Integration:** crate `tests/<topic>.rs` + root `tests/{cli,hook,tui,channel,chaos,contract,security_negatives}_<topic>.rs` (sync, tokio-free; shared helpers in `tests/support/` — the `events.ndjson` reader, its wait, the session-start boot and the one error-body check `error_body_hit` and `assert_error_body_clean` (classes `absolute-path` · `caused-by` · `serde-path` · `planted`, reporting place and class, never bytes) in `events.rs`, the started-child guard and runner in `cli.rs` (every long-lived viola child a root test spawns goes through its tied builder: tied to the spawning test thread by a parent-death kill, exiting when its recorded parent is already gone, spawned only on a thread that outlives it, with the Drop guard's kill then wait still covering the normal end; the census `cross_killed_test_census_finds_no_untied_viola_spawn` fails any other spawn of the viola binary constant) (with `spawn_on` / `viola_on`, which put a planted bin dir on the child's `PATH`; a plain `spawn` of `list` runs with `PATH` set to an empty bin dir, so no test reads the host's `claude` sessions), `empty_bin`, `claude_bin` and `claude_in` in `fake.rs`, the one place a test plants the fake agent as `claude` (a test that plants more than one fake-agent copy plants every copy, each recorded set's bin, one after another before any thread starts a child: on the tmpfs `target/e2e-home` the hard link fails, so each copy is written, and a child one thread forks inherits another thread's open write handle, ETXTBSY), the home-widening helpers `widen` · `grant_read` · `unwiden` · `still_widened` in `home.rs` (Unix modes), through which a root test widens or read-grants a home path, restores it and reads whether it is still widened, the test-owned socket root in `home.rs` (`SOCKET_ROOT_VAR`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`; `SocketRoot`, `Wrapper::boot_on_socket_root` and `first_life_on`, the last there and not beside `first_life` in `start.rs`), the one complete-lines reader in `ndjson.rs` (every reader of a live-appended file parses only newline-terminated lines), the shared start setups in `start.rs` (`first_life`, `wait_session_start_hooks`, `made_dir`, `stopped_life`, `remove_dir_once_free`, `plant_agents`, `listed`, `revive` and `kill_wrapper`), the SGR parser `sgr_attributes` (with `redraws` and `sets_a_foreground`) in `sgr.rs`, its self-check case staying in `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`, the one freeze guard `Frozen` in `frozen.rs` (`attach(pid)` and `Drop`: `kill -STOP`, `ps -o stat=` polled until `T` within `WITHIN`, and `kill -CONT` on drop), and a root test file defines no copy of its own) with `std::process::Command` and jsonschema 0.57.0; each fixed string is pinned by a literal in its test file.

- Steps in order: `cargo build --workspace --features viola/fake-agent` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/harness` (the CLI's `<bin dir>` is `target/harness/debug`) → a not-yet-existing home under `target/e2e-home/viola-session-*/home` (the base first prepared by `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home`: a plain directory is created; a link, as on the Linux dev host, must point at an absolute, real, owner-only directory, made again 0700 when it is gone, and refused when its filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), else `build-failed`) → copy the fake agent to `target/agent-run/<session>/bin/claude` on a harness-scoped `PATH` (per child via `Command::env`) → `viola verify --home` against it with `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root <workspace root> --dialogs --framing`, the fake agent given `--transcript` beside `--framing` (without it Run B's echo probe is skipped and the `local-command-echo` row fails) (print probe + all five interactive runs, Run B with its five added pastes (the long, tag-like and newline texts, then `/compact`, then `/clear`), its one `claude agents --json` read and, on Unix, its one probe `--settings`, and Run E, the `--resume` start of Run B's first session; every relied row, `LedgerRow::relied()`: all twenty-four) unless `--unstamped` → the `--agents-mode recorded|oversize|malformed` value (default `recorded`; a stale file removed before verify) written to the `agents-mode` file beside `bin/claude`, after verify because Run B reads `claude agents --json` through that copy, and recorded as `agents_mode` in `session.json` and `supervise.json` → `viola-harness supervise` as an ordinary child (outlives `boot`; the agent-run CLI's boot leaves it untied, stopping only via `stop.request`; it hands the fake agent `--screens --trusted-root <cwd>`) owning one portable-pty outer PTY per instance via `viola-pty` (master writer kept until the child exits, one drain thread per master).

- No nested `cargo run` inside nextest: tests use `viola_e2e::harness::session::harness_session(test, label, opts) -> HarnessSession` (a plain function and drop guard, never an rstest fixture; the library `boot` spawns the `supervise` process from the given binary dir, tying it and its stamping `viola verify` to the test thread by a parent-death kill; the session is stamped unless `SessionOptions::unstamped`, default false, the in-test form of `boot --unstamped`) or the rstest chain `home → fake_agent_path → stamped_home → booted_wrapper`.

- Root fixture chain: `tests/support/` (`home` → `fake_agent_path` → `stamped_home`, a copy, never a link, of one `viola verify` stamp per build (taken against the fake agent at 2.1.287 over `fixtures/claude`, the fake agent given `--transcript` beside `--framing`, once per pair of built binaries, under an exclusive lock, kept under `target/e2e-home` keyed by the binaries' hashes) → `booted_wrapper`; `StampedHome::unstamped` for the unverified path; every long-lived viola child a root test spawns is tied to its spawning test thread by a parent-death kill (spawned only on a thread that outlives it; exiting when its recorded parent is already gone; `cross_killed_test_census_finds_no_untied_viola_spawn` finds no untied viola spawn in any test source), so a killed or panicked test leaves no wrapper or fake agent, and a Drop guard that kills, then waits, still covers the normal end; `Wrapper::stop` waits for the endpoint to be unconnectable, not only the exit; `wait_ready` at its deadline appends the stalled wrapper's state — its last `run-<name>.ndjson` event, its `/proc/<pid>/wchan` and the `stat` state field (`note_stall`) — to the watch report before the panic, signalling nothing and adding nothing to a passing boot). Homes live under `target/e2e-home/viola-test-*` (the base prepared by `prepare_home_base` under the harness keeper's contract; on the Linux dev host it is a link to an owner-only tmpfs directory, so removals reach outside the working directory and a kept home does not survive a reboot), kept per `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` / `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED` (viola-e2e's booted lifecycle tests: a `Booted` drop guard stops the session, then keeps the home only for a panicking test under `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1`); each records `owner.json` `{pid, started_at}`, and a new home (no keep flag set) first removes only dirs whose recorded owner process is gone — never by age or name, never a dir without a record, save a build's verify stamp dir, which carries none: another build's stamp is swept only when its lock is taken without waiting (a runner-killed test never drops its home); the drop and that sweep both go through `remove_owned`, which deletes `owner.json` last, so a removal that stops part-way keeps the record. The chain exists once, as the sync root copy in `tests/support/`: viola-e2e has no copy and boots its sessions through its own `harness_session`; Path 1's flow lands on the root chain as `tests/path1_run_start.rs`.
